common.name: Name
connections.title: Connections
connections.deleteConfirm: Delete this connection and its stored credentials? Already-uploaded files are not touched.
connections.oauthHint: Providers that use OAuth need no credential fields here — create the connection, then use Authorize below. Configure that provider type's app-wide OAuth client on the Settings page first.
connections.oauthNotConfigured: This provider type needs an app-wide OAuth client before you can authorize a connection.
queue.title: Upload queue
queue.dropZoneHint: Drag files or a folder here, or use the pickers above. Folder structure is preserved on the remote side.
queue.cancelAllConfirm: Cancel every pending and in-flight upload for this connection?
watches.title: Folder watches
watches.intro: Watch a local file or folder on the machine this server runs on, and automatically upload anything created or changed there.
watches.addHint: A newly created watch immediately uploads everything already in the folder, not just future changes.
watches.localPathHint: A path on the server's own machine - type it, since a browser cannot reveal the full path of a picked file or folder.
watches.deleteConfirm: Remove this watch? Already-uploaded files are not affected.
history.title: Upload history
history.deleteConfirm: Remove this entry from the local log? The remote file is not touched.
settings.title: Settings
settings.serverHint: If cloudup's own server served this page, these fields are already filled in — no need to touch this section. They are only needed when running this frontend separately (e.g. npm run dev) against a server on a different origin: that server prints a bearer token to its console on every startup.
settings.serverUrlHint: Leave empty to use this same origin.
settings.savedApplied: Saved — applied immediately, no restart needed.
settings.verifyAfterUploadHint: Per storage type - pick which ones re-check automatically. For a type without a server-side hash this re-downloads every file, doubling upload traffic; for the others it's a cheap metadata check.
settings.verifyAfterUploadExpensive: re-downloads every file to verify (no server-side hash)
settings.multiThreadStreamsHint: Upload a large file's chunks over this many connections at once instead of one at a time (like rclone's --multi-thread-streams). Only S3 and Backblaze B2 support this — Dropbox's protocol cannot. Set to 1 to disable.
settings.multiThreadThresholdMiBHint: Minimum file size before multi-thread streams kick in.
settings.maxUploadKBPerSecondHint: Caps the combined upload rate across every connection at once (like rclone's --bwlimit). 0 means unlimited.
settings.idleConnectionTimeoutMinutesHin: How long a connection may sit with nothing to upload before its background resources are freed - purely internal cleanup, has no effect on uploads themselves. A new one is created automatically the next time it's used.
settings.languageHint: Add more languages by dropping a JSON file into the languages folder next to the executable.
settings.updatesHint: Checks GitHub for the latest release. Only happens when you click the button below - cloudup never checks for updates on its own.
settings.oauthNone: No provider type in this build needs an OAuth client.
settings.oauthClientHint: One Client ID/Secret is shared by every connection of this provider type — create the app once in the provider's developer console and paste its values here. They are stored in the OS keychain on the server and are never readable back, so this page only ever shows whether they are set.
settings.oauthStored: Stored in the OS keychain on the server.
settings.yandexGuide.step1: App type: choose "For user authorization" (recommended for web services) — NOT "For API access or debugging". That other type has a fixed callback URI you can't change, and the type can't be switched after the app is created.
settings.yandexGuide.step2: Platform: check "Web services" — this is what reveals the Callback URI field at all.
settings.yandexGuide.step3: Callback URI — paste this exact value (no trailing slash)
settings.yandexGuide.step4NoAppFolder: sandboxes access to the app's own folder only, incompatible with cloudup's freely chosen upload path
settings.yandexGuide.step5: Fill in any service name and a real contact email (required), then save.
settings.yandexGuide.step6: The resulting ID and Password are your Client ID and Client Secret — paste them below.
